issues.detail: The Greek 'ειπεν προς αυτους' (He said to them) is rendered as 'Người hỏi rằng' (The person asked), changing the action from a statement to a question. Furthermore, the Greek 'ει πνευμα αγιον ελαβετε πιστευσαντες' (if you who have believed received the Holy Spirit) is a conditional statement about receiving, not a question about whether they received it.

The Greek 'αλλ ουδε ει πνευμα αγιον εστιν ηκουσαμεν' (but we have not heard even that it is the Holy Spirit) expresses a lack of hearing/knowledge about the identity or existence of the Spirit, whereas the Vietnamese 'chưa nghe có Thánh Linh nào' implies they haven't heard of any Holy Spirit existing at all.
